text.p: Swedish commercial bank Swedbank said on Wednesday its board intended to propose to pay a dividend of five crowns per share for the 1996 financial year.

The company announced the dividend proposal in connection with its nine-month interim report, which showed an operating profit for the Swedbank group of 3.82 billion crowns, a 23 percent rise on the same 1995 period.
Credit losses for the bank fell to 1.31 billion crowns from 1.80 billion crowns for the first three months of 1995.
Profit before credit losses improved just four percent to 5.12 billion crowns, largely thanks to improved earnings from investment banking operations.

The net of commission income and commission costs rose all of 35 percent to 1.93 billion crowns from 1.43 billion in the first three quarters of last year, and financial transactions contributed 889 million crowns to group income.
Total costs rose a modest three percent to 6.60 billion crowns, much of which was due to an 11 percent increase in administration expenses to 2.52 billion.
Commenting on the result, group CEO Reinhold Geijer said he was pleased with the stability of Swedbank's recent performance.

"I am especially happy about the increase in commission income, and that we as a savings bank are so successful in the area of savings, where (Swedbank's fund manager) Robur as increased its market share substantially this year," he said.
